332	// The cargo-dist shell installer resolves binaries through the archive's

336	function assertInstallableArchiveLayout(name, file) {
337	  if (!(name.endsWith(".tar.xz") || name.endsWith(".tar.gz") || name.endsWith(".tgz"))) {
338	    return;
339	  }
340	  const listing = spawnSync("tar", ["-tf", file], { encoding: "utf8" });
341	  if (listing.status !== 0) {
342	    throw new Error(`tar -tf failed for ${name}: ${listing.stderr}`);
343	  }
344	  for (const member of listing.stdout.split("\n").filter(Boolean)) {
345	    if (member === "." || member === "./" || member.startsWith("./")) {
346	      throw new Error(
347	        `${name} contains './'-prefixed member ${member}; repack with explicit top-level names or the shell installer breaks`,
348	      );
349	    }
350	  }

362	  let verifiedUrls = 0;

379	      }

410	function artifactKind(file) {

465	function releaseFiles(dir, options) {
466	  const entries = [];
467	  walk(dir, (file) => {
468	    const relative = path.relative(dir, file).replaceAll(path.sep, "/");
469	    if (relative === ".DS_Store" || relative.endsWith("/.DS_Store")) {
470	      return;
471	    }
472	    const name = relative.split("/").pop();
473	    if (!isReleaseAsset(name, relative)) {
474	      return;
475	    }
476	    if (!options.includeChecksums && name === "SHA256SUMS") {
477	      return;
478	    }
479	    if (!options.includeManifest && name === "release-manifest.json") {
480	      return;
481	    }
482	    entries.push({ name, relative });
483	  });
484	  entries.sort((a, b) => a.relative.localeCompare(b.relative));
485	  // Published release assets are flat, so every artifact is recorded by its
486	  // basename — users verify downloads with `shasum -a 256 -c SHA256SUMS`
487	  // next to flat files. The CI global-artifact layout nests some files
488	  // twice; identical duplicates collapse, divergent content fails closed.
489	  const byName = new Map();
490	  for (const entry of entries) {
491	    const existing = byName.get(entry.name);
492	    if (existing === undefined) {
493	      byName.set(entry.name, entry);
494	      continue;
495	    }
496	    const existingDigest = sha256(path.join(dir, existing.relative));
497	    const duplicateDigest = sha256(path.join(dir, entry.relative));
498	    if (existingDigest !== duplicateDigest) {
499	      throw new Error(
500	        `conflicting contents for release asset ${entry.name}: ${existing.relative} vs ${entry.relative}`,
501	      );
502	    }
503	  }
504	  return [...byName.values()].sort((a, b) => a.name.localeCompare(b.name));
505	}
506	
507	function walk(dir, visitor) {
508	  if (!fs.existsSync(dir)) {
509	    return;
510	  }
511	  for (const entry of fs.readdirSync(dir, { withFileTypes: true })) {
512	    const fullPath = path.join(dir, entry.name);
513	    if (entry.isDirectory()) {
514	      walk(fullPath, visitor);
515	    } else {
516	      visitor(fullPath);
517	    }
518	  }
519	}
520	
521	function parseChecksums(file) {
522	  const result = new Map();
523	  for (const line of fs.readFileSync(file, "utf8").split(/\r?\n/)) {
524	    if (!line.trim()) {
525	      continue;
526	    }
527	    const match = /^([a-f0-9]{64})\s+(.+)$/.exec(line.trim());
528	    if (!match) {
529	      throw new Error(`invalid SHA256SUMS line: ${line}`);
530	    }
531	    result.set(match[2], match[1]);
532	  }
533	  return result;
534	}

538	    encoding: "utf8",
539	  });
540	  if (output.status === 0) {
541	    return JSON.parse(output.stdout);
542	  }
543	  return {
544	    packages: [
545	      {
546	        name: "deadreckon",
547	        version: workspaceVersion(),
548	        source: null,
549	        license: "MIT",
550	      },
551	    ],
552	  };
553	}
554	
555	function workspaceVersion() {
556	  const text = fs.readFileSync("Cargo.toml", "utf8");
557	  const match = /\[workspace\.package\][\s\S]*?\nversion\s*=\s*"([^"]+)"/.exec(text);
558	  if (!match) {
559	    throw new Error("Cargo.toml [workspace.package] version not found");
560	  }
561	  return match[1];
562	}
563	
564	function wrapperPackageVersion() {
565	  const packageJson = JSON.parse(fs.readFileSync("npm/deadreckon/package.json", "utf8"));
566	  return packageJson.version;
567	}
568	
569	function changelogHasVersion(version, changelogPath) {
570	  if (!fs.existsSync(changelogPath)) {
571	    return false;
572	  }
573	  const escaped = version.replace(/[.*+?^${}()|[\]\\]/g, "\\$&");
574	  return new RegExp(`^##\\s+.*\\b${escaped}\\b`, "m").test(fs.readFileSync(changelogPath, "utf8"));
575	}
576	
577	function safeId(value) {
578	  return value.replace(/[^A-Za-z0-9.-]/g, "-");
579	}
580

583	}
584	
585	function required(value, name) {
586	  if (!value) {

588	  }

590	}

594	}

603	      .filter(([, entry]) => entry === null || ["string", "number", "boolean"].includes(typeof entry))
604	      .map(([key, entry]) => `${key}=${entry ?? ""}`);
605	    fs.appendFileSync(args["github-output"], `${lines.join("\n")}\n`);
606	  }
607	  process.stdout.write(text);

I've now read all three changed files in full and traced the data flow:

**Change summary:** A new `isReleaseAsset()` allowlist filter is added to `releaseFiles()` in `release-trust.mjs`. All consumers (`writeChecksums`, `writeManifest`, `verifyManifest`, `verifyHomebrew`) inherit the same filter through that one entry point, so the SHA256SUMS / release-manifest / homebrew-verify paths stay consistent with each other.

**Cross-checks performed:**
- Confirmed all four `releaseFiles()` callers go through the new filter — no sibling enumeration bypasses it.
- Compared the filter's allowlist against the publish step's `find … -name` allowlist at `.github/workflows/release.yml:434-439`. They match almost exactly (only difference: `.tgz` appears in the JS filter but not in `find`; that's a no-op since the publish step won't upload `.tgz` either).
- Verified the trust-path branch (`relative.startsWith("trust/") || relative.includes("/trust/")`) restricts to `.json`, so a planted `trust/evil.sh` is excluded; nested trust JSONs flow consistently into both manifest write and verify.
- Verified that `walk()` semantics are unchanged; symlink-following behavior is pre-existing.
- The test addition only sets up a loose binary in a per-target dir to assert the new filter excludes it — no security surface.
- The Cargo.toml change is a version bump + a new `inquire` dep (no use-site introduced in this diff).

**Analysis of the fail-closed → fail-open concern:** Previously, a loose binary in a per-target directory (e.g., `deadreckon-aarch64-apple-darwin/deadreckon`) would be hashed into SHA256SUMS and could trigger the conflicting-duplicate-basename failure across mac/linux targets. The new filter silently excludes such intermediates. This *would* be a concern if the publish step uploaded loose binaries — but the publish `find` at release.yml:434 uses the same allowlist (archives, installers, `.rb`, manifests, `trust/*.json`), so the loose binaries are never published. The change brings the verifier into alignment with publish reality rather than opening a verification gap.

No exploitable vulnerability found in this diff.
